symptom: PC in Finance cannot reach another Finance PC; both ports show access mode.
topology_note: SW1 Fa0/10 and Fa0/11 should be access ports in VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
SW1#show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
1 default active Fa0/1, Fa0/10, Fa0/11
10 FINANCE active
SW1#show interfaces fa0/10 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: Access ports Fa0/10 and Fa0/11 are assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10.

symptom: VLAN 20 users can reach their gateway but cannot reach VLAN 30 hosts.
topology_note: R1 provides router-on-a-stick routing on G0/0/0; SW1 uplinks on G0/24.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0/0.20 192.168.20.1 up up
G0/0/0.30 192.168.30.1 up up
SW1#show interfaces g0/24 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20
expected_fault: The switch-to-router link is access VLAN 20 rather than an 802.1Q trunk carrying both VLANs.

symptom: Clients in VLAN 40 self-assign 169.254.x.x addresses.
topology_note: DHCP server is 10.10.100.10 outside the client subnet.
show_outputs:
SW1#show run interface vlan 40
interface Vlan40
 ip address 10.10.40.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
R1#show run interface g0/0/0.40
interface G0/0/0.40
 encapsulation dot1Q 40
 ip address 10.10.40.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: No DHCP relay is configured on the VLAN 40 gateway; clients' broadcasts cannot reach the remote DHCP server.

symptom: Users can ping 8.8.8.8 but web names such as example.com do not resolve.
topology_note: Clients use DHCP-provided DNS server 10.20.0.53.
show_outputs:
PC>ipconfig /all
DNS Servers . . . . . . : 10.20.0.53
PC>ping 8.8.8.8
Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=22ms
R1#show ip route 10.20.0.0
% Network not in table
expected_fault: The DNS server subnet is unreachable because the required route to 10.20.0.0/24 is missing.

symptom: Hosts in 10.50.10.0/24 can communicate locally but cannot leave the subnet.
topology_note: Default gateway should be 10.50.10.1 on the distribution router.
show_outputs:
PC>ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.50.10.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 10.50.10.254
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0/1 10.50.10.1 up up
expected_fault: Clients are configured with the wrong default gateway address.

symptom: A workstation in 10.60.8.0/24 cannot reach 10.60.9.20 even though the remote host is up.
topology_note: Both networks are routed separately as /24 networks.
show_outputs:
PC>ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.60.8.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway: 10.60.8.1
R1#show ip route 10.60.9.0
Routing entry for 10.60.9.0/24
expected_fault: The workstation uses /16 and treats 10.60.9.20 as local, bypassing its router.

symptom: Intermittent connectivity occurs for two devices claiming 10.70.1.50.
topology_note: Access switch Fa0/7 and Fa0/8 connect the two affected endpoints.
show_outputs:
SW1#show mac address-table address 00aa.1111.2222
Vlan Mac Address Type Ports
70 00aa.1111.2222 DYNAMIC Fa0/7
SW1#show ip arp 10.70.1.50
Internet 10.70.1.50  -  00bb.3333.4444 ARPA Vlan70
PC-A>ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.70.1.50
expected_fault: Two endpoints are statically configured with the same IPv4 address, causing ARP instability.

symptom: Branch LAN 10.80.20.0/24 cannot reach the data-center LAN.
topology_note: R2 connects to R1 over 172.16.12.0/30.
show_outputs:
R2#show ip route 10.10.0.0
% Network not in table
R2#show ip interface brief
G0/0 10.80.20.1 up up
G0/1 172.16.12.2 up up
expected_fault: R2 lacks a static route for the data-center network via 172.16.12.1.

symptom: OSPF neighbors remain down and no learned routes appear.
topology_note: R1 and R2 are directly connected on 10.0.12.0/30 and should form area 0 adjacency.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID Pri State Dead Time Address Interface
2.2.2.2 1 EXSTART/- 00:00:31 10.0.12.2 GigabitEthernet0/0
R1#show ip ospf interface g0/0
Network Type: BROADCAST
MTU: 1500
R2#show interface g0/0 | include MTU
MTU 1400 bytes
expected_fault: The OSPF adjacency is stuck in EXSTART because the interface MTUs do not match.

symptom: Users in VLAN 30 cannot access HTTPS on the application server but can ping it.
topology_note: Server is 10.30.10.20; HTTPS uses TCP/443.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists
Extended IP access list USER-FILTER
 10 deny tcp 10.30.30.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.30.10.20 eq 443
 20 permit ip any any
R1#show ip interface g0/0/0.30
Inbound access list is USER-FILTER
expected_fault: An ACL explicitly denies VLAN 30 HTTPS traffic to the application server.

symptom: Inside users can reach internal networks but cannot access the Internet.
topology_note: R1 has inside interface G0/0 and outside interface G0/1.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 0
Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0
Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/1
R1#show run | include ip nat inside source
expected_fault: No inside-source NAT overload rule exists for the 192.168.10.0/24 users.

symptom: Wireless clients associate successfully but receive no IP address.
topology_note: AP uplink is expected to carry the employee SSID VLAN 50.
show_outputs:
AP#show vlan
SSID EMPLOYEE -> VLAN 50
SW1#show interfaces g0/18 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: The AP uplink is in VLAN 1 instead of carrying employee VLAN 50.

symptom: A user replacement laptop is blocked immediately after connection.
topology_note: Fa0/12 should allow one learned MAC address.
show_outputs:
SW1#show port-security interface fa0/12
Port Security: Enabled
Maximum MAC Addresses: 1
Total MAC Addresses: 1
Violation Mode: shutdown
Security Violation Count: 1
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
expected_fault: Port security placed the interface into err-disabled after a MAC-address violation.

symptom: Network operations cannot see the directly connected router in CDP neighbors.
topology_note: R1 G0/0 connects to SW1 G0/1.
show_outputs:
SW1#show cdp interface g0/1
CDP enabled on interface : No
SW1#show cdp neighbors
Device ID Local Intrfce Holdtme Capability Platform Port ID
expected_fault: CDP is disabled on the local interface, so neighbor discovery is unavailable.

symptom: SSH login fails while console access works; Telnet is also unavailable.
topology_note: R1 should accept SSH using local user netadmin.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip ssh
SSH Disabled - version 1.99
R1#show run | section line vty
line vty 0 4
 transport input none
R1#show run | include username|ip domain-name|crypto key
expected_fault: SSH is disabled and VTY lines accept no remote transport; required SSH prerequisites are incomplete.

symptom: New VLAN 60 created on the VTP client disappears after configuration.
topology_note: SW1 is intended to receive VLAN database updates from the VTP server SW2.
show_outputs:
SW1#show vtp status
VTP Operating Mode: Client
VTP Domain Name: CAMPUS
Configuration Revision: 0
SW2#show vtp status
VTP Operating Mode: Server
VTP Domain Name: CAMPUS
Configuration Revision: 12
expected_fault: The VTP client is not receiving the server's VLAN advertisements, so VLAN 60 is not propagated.

symptom: Users experience a loop-related outage after a redundant link is connected.
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 have two parallel Layer-2 links in VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
SW1#show spanning-tree vlan 10
Interface Role Sts Cost
Fa0/23 Root FWD 19
Fa0/24 Desg FWD 19
SW2#show spanning-tree vlan 10
Interface Role Sts Cost
Fa0/23 Desg FWD 19
Fa0/24 Desg FWD 19
expected_fault: STP is not placing one redundant path into a blocking state, indicating an STP topology/control failure.

symptom: Traffic across a bundled uplink is uneven and one member is suspended.
topology_note: SW1 Fa0/21-22 should form a static EtherChannel to SW2.
show_outputs:
SW1#show etherchannel summary
Group Port-channel Protocol Ports
1 Po1(SU) - Fa0/21(P) Fa0/22(s)
SW1#show run interface fa0/22
interface Fa0/22
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
expected_fault: Fa0/22 has different switchport parameters from the bundled interface and is suspended from the EtherChannel.

symptom: Users in the server VLAN lose the default gateway when R1 is rebooted.
topology_note: R1 and R2 provide HSRP for 10.90.10.1.
show_outputs:
R1#show standby brief
Interface Grp Pri P State Active Standby Virtual IP
Gi0/1 10 110 P Active local 10.90.10.2 10.90.10.1
R2#show standby brief
Interface Grp Pri P State Active  Standby  Virtual IP
Gi0/1 10 100 P Active 10.90.10.1 unknown
expected_fault: Both routers report Active because their HSRP peer communication is broken, so failover is not functioning correctly.

symptom: A printer on the Operations floor has no network access after a switch replacement.
topology_note: Printer is connected to SW2 Fa0/15 and should use VLAN 70.
show_outputs:
SW2#show interfaces fa0/15 switchport
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1
SW2#show vlan brief
70 OPERATIONS active Fa0/5, Fa0/6
expected_fault: The printer port is not assigned to the required access VLAN 70.

symptom: VLAN 80 reaches its gateway but cannot reach VLAN 90 after a router configuration change.
topology_note: R1 G0/0/0 is the trunk; VLAN 80 and 90 use subinterfaces.
show_outputs:
R1#show run interface g0/0/0.90
interface G0/0/0.90
 ip address 10.90.90.1 255.255.255.0
R1#show run interface g0/0/0.80
interface G0/0/0.80
 encapsulation dot1Q 80
 ip address 10.80.80.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: The VLAN 90 subinterface is missing its 802.1Q encapsulation statement, so tagged VLAN 90 frames are not mapped to the gateway.

symptom: Only some clients in VLAN 25 receive addresses; the pool becomes exhausted quickly.
topology_note: Pool should serve 10.25.25.0/24 while gateway is 10.25.25.1.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool USERS25
Pool USERS25 : 10.25.25.0/24
Utilization mark (high/low): 100% / 80%
Leased addresses: 254
R1#show run | include ip dhcp excluded-address
ip dhcp excluded-address 10.25.25.1 10.25.25.254
expected_fault: Almost the entire DHCP scope is excluded, leaving only one usable address.

symptom: Internal hostname resolution works inconsistently; clients query an unintended resolver.
topology_note: Corporate DNS is 10.100.0.53 and should be supplied by DHCP.
show_outputs:
PC>ipconfig /all
DNS Servers . . . . . . : 8.8.8.8
R1#show run | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool CORP
 network 10.100.20.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 10.100.20.1
 dns-server 8.8.8.8
expected_fault: DHCP advertises a public DNS server instead of the corporate DNS server, breaking internal name resolution.

symptom: A newly configured router interface is up, but hosts cannot reach the next-hop gateway.
topology_note: Router should use 172.20.1.1/30 on the transit link.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip interface brief
G0/0 172.20.1.5 up up
R2#show ip interface brief
G0/0 172.20.1.2 up up
R1#show ip route 172.20.1.0
C 172.20.1.4/30 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
expected_fault: R1 is addressed in 172.20.1.4/30 while R2 expects 172.20.1.0/30; the two interfaces are in different subnets.

symptom: A host reports intermittent reachability to a remote /24 network after manual TCP/IP configuration.
topology_note: Network standard requires 255.255.255.0 for the 10.110.5.0 subnet.
show_outputs:
PC>ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 10.110.5.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.128
Default Gateway: 10.110.5.1
R1#show ip route 10.110.5.0
C 10.110.5.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
expected_fault: The host uses /25 while the routed LAN is /24, causing incorrect local/remote boundary decisions.

symptom: A remote office can reach headquarters but headquarters cannot return traffic to the office.
topology_note: Office LAN is 10.120.30.0/24 behind R3.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route 10.120.30.0
% Network not in table
R3#show ip route 0.0.0.0
S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 172.16.23.1
expected_fault: The headquarters router has no return route for the remote office subnet.

symptom: Management SSH works from the admin subnet but is denied from the jump host.
topology_note: Only 10.130.10.0/24 should be permitted to TCP/22 on R1.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists MGMT
10 permit tcp 10.130.10.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22
20 deny tcp any any eq 22
R1#show ip interface g0/0
Inbound access list is MGMT
expected_fault: The ACL permits only the admin subnet and explicitly denies SSH from all other sources, including the jump host.

symptom: A server published through static NAT is unreachable from the Internet.
topology_note: Public address 203.0.113.20 should translate to inside server 192.168.200.20.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global Inside local Outside local Outside global
--- 203.0.113.21 192.168.200.20 --- ---
R1#show run | include ip nat inside source static
expected_fault: The static NAT maps the server to 203.0.113.21 instead of the assigned public address 203.0.113.20.

symptom: Clients connected to the guest SSID can access internal servers, violating guest isolation.
topology_note: Guest SSID should be VLAN 200 and isolated from RFC1918 internal networks.
show_outputs:
WLC#show wlan guest
WLAN ID: 20
SSID: GUEST
Interface/VLAN: 200
SW1#show access-lists GUEST-INTERNET
10 permit ip any any
expected_fault: The guest policy ACL permits all traffic, including access to internal networks.

symptom: A phone and PC connected through the same access port causes repeated security violations.
topology_note: Fa0/20 uses a phone passthrough and should permit two secure MAC addresses.
show_outputs:
SW1#show port-security interface fa0/20
Maximum MAC Addresses: 1
Total MAC Addresses: 2
Security Violation Count: 7
Port Status: Secure-shutdown
expected_fault: Port security maximum is one MAC while the design requires two, causing repeated violations and err-disable.
